sanskrit_verse: साक्षिलेख्यानुमानेन प्रकुर्वन् कार्यनिर्णयम् । वितत्येह यशो राजा ब्रह्मणस्याप्नोति विष्टपम् ॥
transliteration: sākṣilekhyānumānena prakurvan kāryanirṇayam | vitatyeha yaśo rājā brahmaṇasyāpnoti viṣṭapam ||
sph_interpretive_translation: The king who resolves matters through direct witness, documented evidence, and logical inference expands his renown in this world and attains the realm of Brahma.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority is realized through alignment with pramāṇa (valid means of knowledge)
Causation arises from conscious engagement with truth-bearing instruments
Capacity-based responsibility requires access to and reliance on verifiable data
Restoration logic operates through clarity of perception and integrity of process
Consciousness alignment occurs when decision-making reflects ontological truth
executable_legal_axioms: IF evidence includes sākṣi (direct witness), lekhyam (documentary proof), OR anumāna (logical inference), THEN judicial action MUST proceed based thereon.
IF a ruler's judgment aligns with pramāṇa, THEN expansion of dharma and reputation follows automatically.
IF legal determination lacks valid pramāṇa support, THEN case resolution SHALL NOT be executed.
IF all parties have capacity to present pramāṇa, THEN failure to do so results in automatic suspension of claim or defense.
IF judgment leads to viṣṭapa (higher ontological state), THEN it confirms alignment with Brahmanic authority.
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, reliance upon sākṣi, lekhyam, and anumāna establishes the threshold for legitimate judicial action. The court’s legitimacy derives solely from its alignment with pramāṇa, not procedural precedent or historical interpretation. Authority rests in the capacity to discern truth through valid cognition, not institutional hierarchy alone.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Nyāya functions through pramāṇa-based causality where correct inference restores balance without recourse to punitive frameworks. Anupūrvaśaḥ ensures that every act of knowing rightly manifests sequentially toward universal harmony. Responsibility is proportional to access to pramāṇa; thus, misjudgment stems from epistemic limitation rather than moral fault. Non-punitive reality rule prevails because error dissolves upon corrected cognition.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Process: Re-establish access to original pramāṇa if obscured or suppressed.
Responsibility Assumption Protocol: Encourage party to voluntarily reaffirm facts through sākṣi, lekhyam, or anumāna.
Capacity Restoration Mechanism: Provide tools or mediation to enable accurate presentation of evidence.
Integrity Reintegration Sequence: Align disputants' consciousness with factual basis of dispute until spontaneous recognition of truth occurs.
final_declaration: This law proceeds exclusively from the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam. Judgment rendered through pramāṇa restores dharma. There is no punishment—only realignment of consciousness with truth. Brahmic authority reigns supreme.
